title: No Competitor Is as Dangerous as an Uncommitted Team Member
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The post claims the greatest threat to an organization is internal: uncommitted team members. Even in strong organizations, fully engaged people are about half of the team or fewer, which the author calls the leader's biggest challenge. There are no silver bullets, but organizations with higher engagement share three threads: a culture of recognition, strong relationships and belonging across the organization, and data-driven feedback on engagement indicators. The author concludes that commitment turns potential into results and that leaders must work to build it.
points: Engaged and committed team members are often half or fewer of a team, even in good organizations.
Recognition for outcomes and the people behind them correlates with commitment.
Belonging and cross-organization relationships are signs of engagement and can be fostered by leaders.
Data-driven feedback on collaboration and involvement helps team members raise their engagement.
quotes: Ask team members to anonymously rate how many of their colleagues are fully engaged and committed to the short and long-range goals of the organization or team, and you are likely to be surprised at the estimate.
Even in the best organizations, team members who are fully engaged and committed represent half or fewer of the team.

Unlike informal appreciation, recognition is more formal and given for achievements, outstanding performance, and the attainment of milestones. Organizations and teams that make a point of recognizing outcomes and the people who create them foster more commitment.
More committed team members feel connected to others and have a strong sense of belonging to the team or organization.

If commitment transforms potential into results, then leaders must do their best to transform commitment. The more team members who are aligned, fully engaged, and committed to the team and its goals, the more success an organization will realize.
